questions.question: Does the change do what was asked on every stated input, including the edge inputs the contract defines?
questions.fails: Any stated input behaves against the issue or contract, or a defined edge input is unhandled.
questions.clears: Every stated input, edges included, behaves as required.
questions.proving_test: Tests asserting each stated input's output, wired to the acceptance criteria.
not_for: Inputs the contract leaves undefined; those belong to a new requirement, not this question.

questions.question: Does every previously supported case keep working, or is each removal declared and tested?
questions.fails: A previously supported input or case stops working with no declaration.
questions.clears: All supported cases work, or each removal is declared with its replacement tested.
questions.proving_test: Regression tests over the previously supported cases.
not_for: Cases never supported; absence there is a feature request, not a regression.

questions.question: Is every error output part of the contract: documented, shaped, and tested?
questions.fails: An error path returns an undocumented shape, code, or message the callers cannot rely on.
questions.clears: Every error output matches its documented shape.
questions.proving_test: Tests asserting each error output's shape and code.
not_for: Log lines and debug output, which carry no contract.

questions.question: Is the change safe when two runs, threads, or tasks use it at once?
questions.fails: Concurrent use corrupts data, loses an update, or lets two holders claim one exclusive thing.
questions.clears: Concurrent use keeps every invariant, shown by a test with two simultaneous actors.
questions.proving_test: A concurrency test with two simultaneous actors over the shared state.
not_for: Single-threaded scripts with no shared state; say so in the declaration.

questions.question: Is the change safe to repeat after a partial failure: retry, interrupt, then rerun?
questions.fails: A retry duplicates an effect, or an interrupt strands state the rerun cannot finish.
questions.clears: Retry then rerun produces exactly one effect from any interruption point.
questions.proving_test: A retry-then-rerun test showing one effect after a mid-operation interruption.
not_for: Read-only operations, which a rerun cannot duplicate.

questions.question: Is every ordering assumption explicit and enforced, never assumed from arrival order?
questions.fails: The code relies on an order that nothing enforces: arrival, delivery, or scheduling order.
questions.clears: Each ordering need is enforced by a lock, a sequence, or an explicit check.
questions.proving_test: An out-of-order delivery test over the assumed sequence.
not_for: Order the platform guarantees, such as a single queue's delivery order.

questions.question: Is outside data validated at every trust boundary before it reaches a decision?
questions.fails: Unvalidated outside data reaches a branch, a query, a command, or stored state.
questions.clears: Each boundary validates shape and range before the data is used.
questions.proving_test: Hostile and malformed input tests at each boundary.
not_for: Data already validated by an earlier boundary in the same call.

questions.question: Does a serialize-and-restore round trip preserve every field the code relies on?
questions.fails: A round trip drops, renames, or alters a relied-upon field or type.
questions.clears: Round trips preserve the relied-upon fields exactly.
questions.proving_test: Round-trip property tests over the serialized forms.
not_for: Display-only formatting, which carries no relied-upon data.

questions.question: Does old stored data keep working: migrations, backfills, and defaults in place?
questions.fails: Old stored data crashes, misbehaves, or silently means something new.
questions.clears: Old versions migrate or default to correct behavior.
questions.proving_test: Old-version fixture tests exercising the migration and defaults.
not_for: A first release with no stored data in the wild.

questions.question: Does every failure surface, never reported as success or complete data?
questions.fails: A failure returns ok, partial data as complete, or an empty result as the answer.
questions.clears: Each failure reaches the caller as a failure with its cause.
questions.proving_test: Fault-injection tests asserting the reported outcome on each failure.
not_for: Best-effort telemetry, whose loss is declared and never load-bearing.

questions.question: Is every acquired resource released on every exit path, including errors?
questions.fails: Any exit path leaks a lock, lease, handle, subscription, or temporary claim.
questions.clears: Every exit path releases what the entry acquired.
questions.proving_test: Exit-path tests asserting release after success and after each failure.
not_for: Resources the runtime owns, such as garbage-collected memory.

questions.question: Are timeouts and cancellation honored, with partial work left finishable?
questions.fails: The code ignores a deadline or cancel signal and runs on, or strands partial work.
questions.clears: Deadlines stop the work and cancellation leaves state the rerun can finish.
questions.proving_test: Cancelled and expired-deadline tests over the long operations.
not_for: Operations that always finish far inside any deadline.

questions.question: Is every caller of changed behavior updated to the new behavior?
questions.fails: A caller still relies on the previous behavior, arguments, or timing.
questions.clears: Each caller is updated and tested against the new behavior.
questions.proving_test: Caller tests exercising the new behavior at each call site.
not_for: Callers outside this change's blast radius; the changed-name search bounds that set.

questions.question: Is every reader of a changed name updated or marked unaffected?
questions.fails: A mention outside the diff still assumes the old name, shape, or meaning.
questions.clears: Each mention is updated or recorded as unaffected with its reason.
questions.proving_test: A clean changed-name search plus reader tests where behavior moved.
not_for: Historical records such as merged release notes, which describe the past.

questions.question: Does the observable contract stay documented where its readers look?
questions.fails: Behavior changed while the documents, examples, or help describing it still show the old.
questions.clears: The documents, examples, and help a reader reaches first describe the new behavior.
questions.proving_test: Documented-example tests plus the changed-name search over the documents.
not_for: Internal notes nobody reads to use the change.

questions.question: Does every action check that this actor may act on that object?
questions.fails: An actor reaches, alters, or learns about a record that is not theirs.
questions.clears: Each action refuses actors without a grant on that object.
questions.proving_test: Cross-actor tests showing refusal on records that are not theirs.
not_for: Truly public data with no per-actor boundary.

questions.question: Is outside text never executed, queried, or commanded: always data, escaped at every sink?
questions.fails: Outside text reaches an interpreter, a query, a shell, or a prompt unescaped.
questions.clears: Each sink treats outside text as data with its escaping tested.
questions.proving_test: Injection-string tests per sink, including the odd encodings.
not_for: Text the operator typed themselves into their own shell.

questions.question: Is every file the change creates readable only by those who need it?
questions.fails: A created file, especially one bearing secrets or personal data, is readable beyond its need.
questions.clears: Created files carry least-privilege permissions.
questions.proving_test: Permission assertions on the files the change creates.
not_for: Files the platform creates and owns, such as package caches.

questions.question: Does every secret come from configuration or a secret store, never from code, logs, or output?
questions.fails: A secret sits in code, ships in output, or lands in a log.
questions.clears: Secrets arrive only from configuration or the secret store, and leave no copies.
questions.proving_test: Configuration-only sourcing tests plus a clean secret scan of the diff.
not_for: Inert example values in tests and documents, which unlock nothing.

questions.question: Does every new outbound path carry only its intended data, redacted where it must be?
questions.fails: Personal or sensitive data leaves on a new path, or leaves unredacted where redaction applies.
questions.clears: Each outbound path is enumerated with its data and its redaction.
questions.proving_test: Redaction tests on each new outbound path.
not_for: Paths the change does not touch; those were reviewed when they were built.

questions.question: Is everything the change brings in pinned, reviewed, and minimal?
questions.fails: A new dependency, plugin, action, or image is unpinned, unreviewed, or broader than needed.
questions.clears: Each addition is pinned, reviewed for its reach, and the smallest that does the job.
questions.proving_test: Pin and lockfile checks plus a review note per addition.
not_for: The toolchain itself, which the repository profile pins once.

questions.question: Is every granted permission minimal, named, and exercised?
questions.fails: A grant is broader than the code uses, unused, or unnamed in the change.
questions.clears: Each grant names its need and the code exercises exactly it.
questions.proving_test: Grant-enumeration tests showing each grant used and none spare.
not_for: Permissions the platform grants by default with no request from the change.

questions.question: Does a test run every changed branch?
questions.fails: A changed branch runs in no test.
questions.clears: Changed-line branch coverage is complete, or each gap is recorded unreachable with its reason.
questions.proving_test: The changed-line branch coverage report.
not_for: Unchanged lines; the question is only about what this change adds.

questions.question: Do the tests fail without the fix and pass with it?
questions.fails: A new test passes on the code before the change, or a regression test passes before its fix.
questions.clears: The two runs show red before and green after.
questions.proving_test: The two-runs check over the new and regression tests.
not_for: Tests for behavior this change does not touch.

questions.question: Do the tests exercise the real code under test, not a fake of it?
questions.fails: A double replaces the unit under test, so the test passes while the code is wrong.
questions.clears: Doubles stand only at the boundary; the unit under test runs for real.
questions.proving_test: Mutation testing over the changed lines plus review of the doubles.
not_for: Doubles at the system boundary, such as a fake clock or a stubbed service.

questions.question: Does every test stay inside its sandbox: no live or shared system written or read?
questions.fails: A test writes to, or depends on, a live or shared system.
questions.clears: Tests run network-blocked against sandbox doubles only.
questions.proving_test: Network-blocked test runs over the suite.
not_for: Read-only fixtures committed with the repository.

questions.question: Does the change follow the recorded decisions and patterns, or record the new one it sets?
questions.fails: The change contradicts the repository instructions or a recorded decision with no new record.
questions.clears: The change fits the records, or carries its decision record with it.
questions.proving_test: The builder's declaration against the records; no tool judges prose fit.
not_for: Brand-new ground with no recorded pattern; that is a decision to write, not a breach.

questions.question: Does every machine-specific value come from configuration, never baked into the code?
questions.fails: An absolute path, user name, host, account, or address sits in the code outside configuration.
questions.clears: Machine values arrive only from configuration with documented defaults.
questions.proving_test: The machine-values search plus the relocated test run.
not_for: Loopback and documentation addresses, which name no real machine.

questions.question: Does the change add no second copy of a value, list, or rule?
questions.fails: A value, list, or rule now lives in two places that can disagree.
questions.clears: Each value, list, and rule has one home the change reuses.
questions.proving_test: The duplication report over the changed lines.
not_for: Copies that must disagree, which are a correctness question about the old behavior.

questions.question: Do the tests pass from a different working directory and home directory?
questions.fails: The relocated run fails: the tests assumed the author's directories.
questions.clears: The relocated run passes.
questions.proving_test: The relocated test run in the build loop.
not_for: Tests that must assert on the real home, which say so and are few.
